'''Jinyoung Park''' ({{Korean|hangul=박진영}}; born 1982) is a South Korean [[mathematician]] at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] working in [[combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]].

She and Huy Tuan Pham proved the [[Kahn–Kalai conjecture]] on estimating the positions of [[phase transition]]s in [[statistical mechanics]] and [[random graph]] theory.<ref name=Quanta>{{Cite web |last=Cepelewicz |first=Jordana |date=2022-04-25 |title=Elegant Six-Page Proof Reveals the Emergence of Random Structure |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/elegant-six-page-proof-reveals-the-emergence-of-random-structure-20220425/ |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=[[Quanta Magazine]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Park entered [[Seoul National University]] in 2001 and received her B.S. in Mathematics Education in 2004. She worked as a mathematics teacher in secondary schools in [[Seoul]] from 2005 to 2011. She began her graduate studies at [[Rutgers University]] in 2014,<ref name=Homepage>{{Cite web |title=Curriculum vitae |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-9F5mGcRlQDRt0I5U6lXEpGP-ATCmknm/view |access-date=2024-10-21}} As linked from Park's home page.</ref> where she received her Ph.D. in 2020 under the supervision of [[Jeff Kahn (mathematician)|Jeff Kahn]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|282087}}</ref> Her doctoral work earned the 2022 Dissertation Prize from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-dissertation-prize/awm-dissertation-prize-2022/ |title=AWM Dissertation Prize 2022 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics |date=2022 |access-date=2022-05-09}}</ref>

She was a Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2020 to 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jinyoung-park |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |title=Jinyoung Park |date=4 March 2020 |access-date=2022-05-09}}</ref> From 2021 to 2022 she was a Szegö Assistant Professor at Stanford University, where her postdoctoral mentor was [[Jacob Fox]].<ref name=Homepage/> She joined the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] in 2023, where she is currently an assistant professor.<ref name=Homepage/><ref name=CourantFaculty>{{Cite web |title=Faculty List at the Courant Institute |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/people/faculty/ |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=[[Courant Institute]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2023, Park received the [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]] "for contributions to the resolution of several major conjectures on thresholds and selector processes".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Winners Of The 2023 Breakthrough Prizes In Life Sciences, Mathematics And Fundamental Physics Announced |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/73 |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, she received the [[Dénes König Prize]] together with her coauthor Huy Tuan Pham, "for their outstanding research in discrete mathematics, in special recognition of their ingenious, short, and surprising proof of the Kahn–Kalai conjecture".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jinyoung Park and Huy Tuan Pham|work=2024 July Prize Spotlight
 |url=https://www.siam.org/publications/siam-news/articles/2024-july-prize-spotlight#Park-Pham |access-date=2024-03-12 |publisher=SIAM |language=en}}</ref> The following year, she was the 2025 recipient of the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]], given for her article "Threshold phenomena for random discrete structures" in the ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7374|title=Park Awarded 2025 Conant Prize|date=October 17, 2024|work=News from the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-10-21}}</ref>
